plan.hypothesis: Increasing control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from the incumbent 0.05 toward the frozen upper bound 0.10, keeping control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at 0.05, lowers nominal holding_max_speed_m_s below 0.012750255515948416 m/s while keeping holding_max_error_m and terminal_error_m at or below 0.01 m.
plan.rationale: Frozen control domains admit only control/recipe/{terminal,holding}_tip_speed_weight in [0.025,0.1]; both are 0.05 in the incumbent. The holding term is a per-second squared normalized world tip speed on nodes at/after the fixed settling-window start (0.3-0.35 s), so it is the direct pressure on the only failed component (holding speed). Mathematical support is limited: a monotone penalty term is expected to lower in-window tip speed, but the effect on the sampled maximum and its interaction with position/terminal cost is not analytically guaranteed, and the incumbent already passes, so only response direction and trade-off can be observed. Two interior points 0.075 and 0.10 bracket the lever for a within-batch slope estimate; per-batch backend cap is two. No robustness or superiority claim is licensed because perturbation cases are unexecutable and near_z_plus is a non-matched subsequent event.

decision.reasoning: Current feedback: the incumbent nominal execution 91c3ba1b01d6499fb26df8f95409401b is accepted (F104=true) with holding_max_speed 0.012750255515948416 m/s vs limit 0.02 (F14<F31), holding_max_error 0.0027300544346297905 m and terminal_error 0.002697828858325615 m, both under 0.01 (F1,F108), coverage true (F100), solver errors 0 (F115). The only exposed non-matched subsequent event (near_z_plus, candidate shared-path-v11-near-section-096) is a valid_failure (F75) driven solely by holding speed 0.06758272073425946 m/s > 0.02 (F46>F31, F92=false). Because the perturbation cases are unavailable for execution in this pilot and only nominal is runnable, the robust question cannot be answered by structure change; instead the targeted, cheapest testable control-response uncertainty is whether the frozen holding-window tip-speed penalty actually lowers in-window tip speed. Both control paths lie in frozen [0.025,0.1]; I vary only control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight above the incumbent 0.05, holding terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at 0.05. Two interior points bracket the lever and estimate slope within the two-backend per-batch cap, leaving two solves for feedback and the final decision.

No repeatability or variance evidence exists for any configuration.

interpretations.statement: The original first-decision hypothesis is contradicted at nominal: raising control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight above the incumbent 0.05 raised, not lowered, holding-window tip speed, while holding position and terminal reach stayed within tolerance.
interpretations.uncertainty: One execution per point; the weight-to-speed relation is not established as monotone or causal; acceptance is a sampled nominal result only.

decision.reasoning: The original first decision proposed control_search raising control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from 0.05 to {0.075,0.10} with control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at 0.05, predicting holding_max_speed_m_s below the incumbent 0.012750255515948416 m/s while keeping holding_max_error_m and terminal_error_m at or below 0.01 m. Both newly completed pilot executions now falsify that direction on the nominal case: the 0.075 point (F75=0.023285947509969908) and the 0.10 point (F71=0.022128674933740447) both exceed the 0.02 m/s holding-speed limit and are the only failing component (F188=false, F173=false), while reach and holding position pass (F129=F131=true; F63=F69=true) and both terminal (F113=0.002633323294646377, F215=0.0028347191207395775) and holding position (F125=0.0028109103441942935, F146=0.002905756064671871) stay under 0.01. So raising the holding penalty raised, not lowered, in-window tip speed; the incumbent (F122=0.012750255515948416, F156=accepted) keeps the best margin. The two pilot points also reproduce the matched historical failures at the same scientific configuration identities (holding 0.075: F75=F166 equal; holding 0.10: F71=F89 equal), so they add replication of a known failure rather than a new signal; the original replication_reason was null and no repetition intent is inferred. The passing joint-weight point (F7=0.010201160469407439, F79=accepted, holding 0.09 with terminal 0.10) is confounded by the simultaneous terminal change and cannot attribute the speed reduction to any single lever. The frozen question concerns robustness to prescribed small initial-state variation, but only the zero-perturbation nominal case is executable here (the four perturbation cases are deferred and the local numerical saved-state route is an explicit capability gap), so no currently legal executable action can address that robustness uncertainty. Given the refuted lever, the unreachable robustness route, and an already-accepted incumbent, further nominal-only spending has little scientific value. This is a voluntary model STOP, not an acceptance/optimality/robustness/causality claim.
decision.stop_reason: Original holding-weight hypothesis falsified by its own pilot outcomes (both higher-weight points fail the holding-speed acceptance that the hypothesis targeted while position/terminal pass); the two points merely replicate known matched failures; the frozen perturbation-robustness question has no legal executable route in this context; and an already-accepted incumbent exists, so further nominal-only evidence has little value. Voluntary model STOP.
